text_blocks.snippet: Greta Thunberg has spoken openly about having Asperger's syndrome, which is now considered part of the autism spectrum disorder, as well as obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). She has also discussed struggling with an eating disorder and selective mutism. While acknowledging that these conditions have presented challenges, she has also described her neurodivergence as a "superpower" that fuels her climate activism.

list.title: Asperger's Syndrome/Autism Spectrum Disorder:
list.snippet: Thunberg was diagnosed with Asperger's syndrome around the age of 11, which is now classified under autism spectrum disorder. She has described how this diagnosis has shaped her perspective and approach to activism.

list.title: Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD):
list.snippet: Thunberg has also been open about having OCD. She has indicated that her intense focus on climate change, which is a defining characteristic of her activism, is partly due to her OCD and her ability to hyper-focus on a single issue.

list.title: Eating Disorder:
list.snippet: Thunberg's mother has described how she struggled with an eating disorder, including periods of not eating and losing a significant amount of weight.

list.title: Selective Mutism:
list.snippet: Thunberg has also mentioned having selective mutism, which means she only speaks when she feels it is necessary.

list.title: "Superpower":
list.snippet: Despite the challenges, Thunberg views her neurodivergence as a strength. She has described it as a "superpower" that enables her to see the world in a unique way and to be a powerful advocate for climate action.
